_doc: Model registry for enough.
Seven supported local LLMs, keyed by a short 'cute name' the user sees
in the UI and can pass as MODEL=<name> to llama_server.sh:
G40-04 — Gemma 4 4B (E4B MatFormer), ~5 GB
Q35-09 — Qwen3.5-9B, ~6 GB (MTP build)
G40-12 — Gemma 4 12B, ~7 GB (quantization-aware-trained q4_0)
G40-26 — Gemma 4 26B MoE (4B active), ~16 GB
Q36-27 — Qwen3.6-27B dense, ~17 GB (MTP build)
Q38-04 — Qwen3.8-27B at 4-bit, ~19 GB + a ~1.7 GB MTP draft
Q38-16 — Qwen3.8-27B at 16-bit, ~54 GB + a ~3.2 GB MTP draft
Naming caution: the numeric suffix means PARAMETER COUNT on the
gemma-4 / qwen-3.5 / qwen-3.6 entries but QUANT BITS on the two
qwen-3.8 ones (g40-04 = 4B params; q38-04 = 4-bit). The 'label'
field carries the disambiguation — never render the cute name alone.
Each entry declares its GGUF download URL + filename, approximate
disk footprint, minimum recommended RAM, and a ctx_default table
that maps total-RAM tiers to a recommended context window. Those
defaults are starting points; the live config can override per model.
An optional top-level 'llama_cpp_min_release' is a HARD gate: the
b-release of llama.cpp below which the model's architecture cannot
be loaded at all. Absent or 0 means no gate. enough.models.release_gate()
turns it into a friendly 'brew upgrade llama.cpp' error; both the
supervisor and llama_server.sh refuse to launch below it, rather
than letting llama-server fail with an opaque tensor error.
An optional 'mtp' block marks models that support Multi-Token
Prediction speculative decoding. Two shapes, both behind the same
spec_type/spec_draft_n_max keys:
- EMBEDDED heads (q35-09, q36-27): the MTP tensors ride inside the
main GGUF, so the block is flags only. The Qwens use MTP-preserving
GGUFs from unsloth; note their local gguf_filename carries an
-MTP- marker so a pre-MTP file left in ~/enough/weights/ is never
mistaken for the MTP build.
- SEPARATE draft file (q38-04, q38-16): the MTP head ships as its
own GGUF, named by draft_gguf_filename / draft_gguf_url /
draft_disk_gb_approx. It lands in ~/enough/weights/ beside the
main file and is passed with --spec-draft-model.
The 'mtp' block's own llama_cpp_min_release is a SOFT gate on the
spec flags only: too old, or draft file simply not downloaded, and
the model launches plain. MTP is always a speed bonus, never a
requirement, so 'installed' is derived from the main GGUF alone.
To add a new model, copy an entry and rename its key. Put the new
entry in ~/enough/config/models.json (the live file) — edits to
this template only affect future installs.
Live state is at ~/enough/config/models.json and tracks only:
{ "current": "<cute-name>" }
Installed-state is derived from whether the .gguf file exists at
~/enough/weights/<gguf_filename>. Which models a given machine can
actually run is NOT stored here — enough.models.feasibility() derives
it live from ram_gb_recommended_min + disk_gb_approx vs this host.
